content:
In the past few days, two reports have suggested that Apple could boost its profits by increasing services revenue in different ways.

In my view, Apple absolutely should pursue the first approach, but should not adopt the second — and it seems Phil Schiller may well agree with this stance...

Let me first summarise the content of these two reports.

Home Security and Monitoring Service

On Friday, *Bloomberg* reported that Apple may be planning to launch a brand-new home security and monitoring service, debuting alongside some of the new home hardware we have been expecting.

Extracting More Revenue from the App Store

Another report from the same source on Sunday indicated that the company is exploring ways to extract more revenue and profit from the App Store.

Apple Should Not Take the Latter Approach

Conversely, I believe the second approach would be a massive mistake.

Apple's effective monopoly over iPhone app sales has come under fierce attack from regulators around the world. In most countries, if you want to sell an app on an iPhone, you have to go through the official App Store, leaving you with no choice but to accept the company's terms.

I understand the common argument that no one is forcing anyone to buy an iPhone or develop apps for it, but that is not how even the most laissez-faire free-market economies actually work — the US has had antitrust laws since 1890. Once you reach a certain level of market dominance, regulators impose restrictions on your conduct to ensure you do not abuse your position.

Trying to squeeze more money out of the App Store runs exactly counter to "skating to where the puck is going." According to *Bloomberg*, Phil Schiller shares this view, and notes that it is one of the reasons for his current stepping back.

Innovative Services Are the Right Direction

By contrast, launching innovative services that people are happy to pay for is absolutely what Apple should be doing. I can easily see the value in the company offering a home security monitoring service.

I argued back in 2024 that developing its own smart home cameras would be one of the... wisest moves the company could make. I expressed the same view regarding rumours of an Apple smart doorbell. Offering an optional service bundle to go with security products makes sense on both fronts.

First, there are the privacy reasons I have mentioned many times before. HomeKit Secure Video has already made a major contribution to ensuring the privacy of security camera footage. If I had to pick one company I would trust to analyse security camera footage with AI, it would be Apple.

Second, Apple is of course best positioned to fully integrate security hardware and services within the HomeKit ecosystem. I am confident Apple can deliver similar benefits in many other areas as well.

For me, the key point is that Apple needs to treat services with the same approach it applies to hardware — build outstanding products that consumers are happy and willing to pay for, rather than extracting money in ways that leave customers, developers, and regulators alike unhappy.

What are your thoughts? Feel free to share your views in the comments.
